answer: Northwind retired two forms in 2026, both on February 1, 2026. NW-ODO-1 (Odometer statement) was replaced by NW-ODO-2 (Odometer disclosure statement). NW-POA-1 (Power of attorney, notarized) was replaced by NW-POA-2 (Power of attorney, e-sign), which can be signed electronically with no notary, except in Georgia, where a notary is still required. An NW-POA-1 signed before February 1, 2026 was accepted until June 30, 2026, so that grace period has now ended. Also note that the 'Broken or replaced odometer' article still tells customers to use NW-ODO-1, which is out of date. Customers should use NW-ODO-2 instead.
